Write-Ahead Logging
SQLite supports a WAL mode
that allows concurrent reads
and writes to the database.
The WAL file stores changes
before they are committed.
This improves performance
for write-heavy workloads.
The checkpoint process moves
data from the WAL back to
the main database file.
WAL mode is the default
for most SQLite operations.
It provides better concurrency
than the rollback journal.
Multiple readers can access
the database simultaneously
while a single writer proceeds.
The WAL checkpoint can run
automatically or manually.
It scans the WAL file for
completed transactions and
applies them to the database.
After checkpointing, the WAL
file can be truncated or
reused for new transactions.
The WAL index file stores
shared memory used by readers
to determine which pages
have been modified by writers.
This allows lock-free reads
in most common scenarios.
